passages.title: My Family
passages.text:
Hi, I am Tom. I am ten years old. There are four people in my family. My father is a {doctor}. My mother is a teacher.
I have a little sister. Her name is Amy. She is six. She {likes} cats. We have a cat, Mimi. Mimi is fat and cute. I {love} my family.

cloze.exp: a + 單數職業名詞：a doctor 一位醫生。
主詞 She 是第三人稱單數，動詞加 s：likes。
主詞 I 搭配原形動詞：I love my family.

qs.q: How old is Tom?
qs.exp: I am ten years old.

qs.q: What does Tom's mother do?
qs.exp: My mother is a teacher.

qs.q: Who is Mimi?
qs.exp: We have a cat, Mimi.

tr: 嗨，我是湯姆。
我十歲。
我家有四個人。
我爸爸是醫生。
我媽媽是老師。
我有一個妹妹。
她的名字是艾咪。
她六歲。
她喜歡貓。
我們養了一隻貓，叫咪咪。
咪咪胖胖的，很可愛。
我愛我的家人。

passages.title: At the Zoo
passages.text:
Today is Sunday. Ben and his dad go to the zoo. They see many animals.
The elephant is big. It has a long {nose}. The monkeys are funny. They {jump} and play in the trees.
Ben's favorite animal is the panda. It is black and {white}. It eats bamboo all day. Ben is very happy today.

cloze.exp: 大象有長長的「鼻子」：a long nose。
主詞 They 是複數，用原形動詞 jump。
貓熊是黑「白」色的：black and white。

qs.q: Where do Ben and his dad go?
qs.exp: Ben and his dad go to the zoo.

qs.q: What do the monkeys do?
opts: They jump and play in the trees.
qs.exp: They jump and play in the trees.

qs.q: What is Ben's favorite animal?
qs.exp: Ben's favorite animal is the panda.

tr: 今天是星期日。
班和他爸爸去動物園。
他們看到很多動物。
大象很大。
牠有長長的鼻子。
猴子很好笑。
牠們在樹上跳來跳去、玩耍。
班最喜歡的動物是貓熊。
牠是黑白色的。
牠整天都在吃竹子。
班今天非常開心。

passages.title: Mary's Day
passages.text:
Mary gets up at six thirty every day. She {washes} her face and brushes her teeth. At seven, she eats breakfast with her mom. She has bread and milk.
Then she goes to school {by} bus. School starts at eight. After school, Mary does her homework. She goes to {bed} at nine.

cloze.exp: every day 表習慣，主詞 She 用第三人稱單數 washes。
by bus 搭公車（by + 交通工具）。
go to bed 上床睡覺。

qs.q: What time does Mary get up?
qs.exp: Mary gets up at six thirty every day.

qs.q: What does Mary have for breakfast?
qs.exp: She has bread and milk.

qs.q: How does Mary go to school?
qs.exp: she goes to school by bus.

tr: 瑪莉每天六點半起床。
她洗臉、刷牙。
七點的時候，她和媽媽一起吃早餐。
她吃麵包、喝牛奶。
然後她搭公車上學。
學校八點開始上課。
放學後，瑪莉寫功課。
她九點上床睡覺。

passages.title: What's in My Bag?
passages.text:
My name is Sam. I am a fourth grader. Every morning, I {put} my books in my school bag. There are four books in it: Chinese, English, math, and science. I also have a pencil box. There are three pencils, two erasers, and a ruler {in} it.
My bag is blue and {heavy}. My mom always says, "Don't put toys in your bag!" But today I have a small robot in it. Shh! It's a {secret}. I want to show it to my friend Ken after lunch.

cloze.exp: 主詞 I 搭配原形動詞：I put my books...。
鉛筆放在鉛筆盒「裡面」：in it。
裝了四本書，書包很「重」：heavy。
不想讓媽媽知道，所以是「祕密」：It's a secret.

qs.q: How many books are in Sam's bag?
qs.exp: There are four books in it: Chinese, English, math, and science.

qs.q: What is NOT in Sam's pencil box?
qs.exp: 鉛筆盒裡有鉛筆、橡皮擦和尺；機器人是放在書包裡。

qs.q: Why does Sam say "Shh!"?
opts: He doesn't want his mom to know about the robot.
qs.exp: 媽媽說不要帶玩具，但他偷偷帶了機器人，所以說這是祕密。

qs.q: When does Sam want to show the robot to Ken?
qs.exp: I want to show it to my friend Ken after lunch.

tr: 我的名字是山姆。
我是四年級生。
每天早上，我把書放進書包。
書包裡有四本書：國語、英文、數學和自然。
我也有一個鉛筆盒。
鉛筆盒裡有三枝鉛筆、兩個橡皮擦和一把尺。
我的書包是藍色的，而且很重。
媽媽總是說：「不要把玩具放進書包！」
但是今天我的書包裡有一個小機器人。
噓！
這是祕密。
我想在午餐後拿給我的朋友肯看。

passages.title: Lucky, My Dog
passages.text:
I have a dog. His name is Lucky. He is three years old. He is brown and white, and he has big ears. Lucky can run fast, and he {can} swim, too. But he can't climb trees.
Every evening, my dad and I {walk} Lucky in the park. He likes to play with a ball. When I throw the ball, he runs and brings it {back} to me.
Lucky is very smart. When I am sad, he sits next to me and puts his head on my leg. He is not only my pet. He is my {best} friend.

cloze.exp: 與前句 can run fast 對應：he can swim, too。
主詞 my dad and I 是複數，Every evening 表習慣，用原形 walk（遛狗）。
bring it back 把它帶回來。
my best friend 我最好的朋友。

qs.q: What can't Lucky do?
qs.exp: But he can't climb trees.

qs.q: When do they walk Lucky?
qs.exp: Every evening, my dad and I walk Lucky in the park.

qs.q: What does Lucky do when the writer is sad?
opts: He sits next to the writer.
qs.exp: When I am sad, he sits next to me and puts his head on my leg.

qs.q: Which sentence is true?
opts: Lucky walks alone in the park.
qs.exp: He is brown and white, and he has big ears. 他三歲、棕白色，和爸爸、作者一起散步。

tr: 我有一隻狗。
牠的名字叫樂奇。
牠三歲。
牠是棕白色的，有一對大耳朵。
樂奇跑得很快，牠也會游泳。
但是牠不會爬樹。
每天傍晚，爸爸和我會帶樂奇去公園散步。
牠喜歡玩球。
當我把球丟出去，牠會跑去把球帶回來給我。
樂奇非常聰明。
當我難過的時候，牠會坐在我旁邊，把頭靠在我的腿上。
牠不只是我的寵物。
牠是我最好的朋友。

passages.title: Four Seasons
passages.text:
There are four seasons in a year: spring, summer, fall, and winter. Which one do you like?
In spring, it is warm, and there are many flowers. In summer, it is hot and sunny. Many people go to the beach to {swim}. In fall, it is cool and windy. It is a good time to fly a kite. In winter, it is cold. People wear coats and {drink} hot tea.
My sister likes summer {because} she loves ice cream. I like winter best. Why? My birthday is in December, and I can get many presents! What {about} you?

cloze.exp: 去海邊「游泳」：go to the beach to swim。
主詞 People 複數用原形；喝熱茶用 drink（不能 eat tea）。
喜歡夏天的「原因」是愛吃冰淇淋：because。
What about you? 那你呢？

qs.q: Which season is cool and windy?
qs.exp: In fall, it is cool and windy.

qs.q: Why does the writer's sister like summer?
qs.exp: My sister likes summer because she loves ice cream.

qs.q: When is the writer's birthday?
qs.exp: My birthday is in December.

qs.q: What is a good thing to do in fall?
qs.exp: In fall... It is a good time to fly a kite.

tr: 一年有四個季節：春、夏、秋、冬。
你喜歡哪一個呢？
春天很溫暖，有很多花。
夏天又熱又晴朗。
很多人去海邊游泳。
秋天涼爽、風很大。
這是放風箏的好時節。
冬天很冷。
人們穿外套、喝熱茶。
我姊姊喜歡夏天，因為她超愛冰淇淋。
我最喜歡冬天。
為什麼呢？
我的生日在十二月，我可以收到很多禮物！
那你呢？

passages.title: At the Bookstore
passages.text:
Today is Sunday. Amy and her brother Ben go to a bookstore. Amy wants {to} buy a storybook. Ben wants a comic book.
"How much is this storybook?" Amy asks. "It's 150 dollars," says the clerk. Ben's comic book is 80 dollars. They have 300 dollars. "We can buy them both," Ben says. "And we still have {some} money."
After that, they go to the store next door and buy two cups of juice. Each cup is 35 dollars. Now they {have} no money, but they are very happy. They go home and read their new books {together}.

cloze.exp: want to + 原形動詞：wants to buy。
肯定句中表示「一些」錢用 some；money 不可數，不能用 many 或 a。
主詞 they 是複數，用 have：they have no money。
兄妹兩人「一起」看新書：together。

qs.q: How much is Ben's comic book?
qs.exp: Ben's comic book is 80 dollars.

qs.q: How much money do they have after they buy the two books?
How much do they pay for the juice?
qs.exp: 兩杯果汁，每杯 35 元：35 × 2 = 70 元，剛好把剩下的錢用完。

qs.q: What do Amy and Ben do at home?
qs.exp: They go home and read their new books together.

tr: 今天是星期日。
艾咪和她的哥哥班去書店。
艾咪想買一本故事書。
班想要一本漫畫書。
「這本故事書多少錢？」艾咪問。
班的漫畫書是 80 元。
他們有 300 元。
「我們兩本都買得起，」班說。
「而且還會剩一些錢。」
之後，他們到隔壁的店買了兩杯果汁。
每杯 35 元。
現在他們沒有錢了，但是他們非常開心。
他們回家，一起看新買的書。

passages.title: A Sunny Afternoon
passages.text:
It is a sunny afternoon. Many people are at the park. Look! A girl is {flying} a kite. Her kite looks like a big red bird. Two boys are playing basketball. Their dog is running {after} the ball, too.
Under a big tree, an old man is reading a newspaper. Next to him, a woman is {feeding} the birds. A little boy is crying because he dropped his ice cream. His mother says, "Don't cry. I {will} buy you another one."
What a nice afternoon in the park!

cloze.exp: 現在進行式 is + V-ing：is flying a kite。
run after 追著跑。
現在進行式 is + V-ing：is feeding the birds。
媽媽答應等一下「會」再買一個：will + 原形動詞。

qs.q: What does the girl's kite look like?
qs.exp: Her kite looks like a big red bird.

qs.q: What is the old man doing?
qs.exp: an old man is reading a newspaper. 餵鳥的是旁邊的女士。

qs.q: Why is the little boy crying?
qs.exp: A little boy is crying because he dropped his ice cream.

qs.q: What is the weather like?
qs.exp: It is a sunny afternoon.

tr: 這是一個晴朗的午後。
公園裡有很多人。
你看！
一個女孩正在放風箏。
她的風箏看起來像一隻紅色的大鳥。
兩個男孩正在打籃球。
他們的狗也在追著球跑。
一棵大樹下，有位老先生正在看報紙。
在他旁邊，一位女士正在餵鳥。
一個小男孩在哭，因為他的冰淇淋掉了。
他媽媽說：「別哭。
我會再買一支給你。」
公園裡的午後真美好！

passages.title: My Birthday Party
passages.text:
Last Saturday was my birthday. I was eleven years old. My friends {came} to my house for a party. My mom {made} a big chocolate cake. We sang a birthday song, and I made a wish.
My best friend, Kelly, gave me a storybook. My grandpa {gave} me a new watch. After that, we played games and ate pizza. Everyone had a good {time}. It was the best birthday ever!

cloze.exp: Last Saturday 是過去時間，come 的過去式為 came。
做蛋糕用 make，過去式 made。
give sb. sth. 給某人某物，過去式 gave。
have a good time 玩得很愉快。

qs.q: How old was the writer on this birthday?
qs.exp: I was eleven years old.

qs.q: What did Kelly give the writer?
qs.exp: Kelly, gave me a storybook.

qs.q: What did they eat at the party?
qs.exp: 媽媽做了巧克力蛋糕，後來大家 ate pizza。

tr: 上星期六是我的生日。
我滿十一歲了。
朋友們來我家參加派對。
媽媽做了一個大大的巧克力蛋糕。
我們唱了生日歌，我許了願。
我最好的朋友凱莉送我一本故事書。
爺爺送我一支新手錶。
之後，我們玩遊戲、吃披薩。
每個人都玩得很開心。
這是我過過最棒的生日！

passages.title: A Rainy Day
passages.text:
It is rainy today, so Leo can't play basketball in the park. He is a little sad. He sits by the window and {looks} at the rain.
His mother says, "Why don't you read a book?" Leo finds an old book about dinosaurs. The book has many {pictures}. Leo learns that some dinosaurs were as tall as a house! He reads for two hours.
When the rain stops, Leo is not sad {anymore}. He wants to {visit} the science museum this weekend to see the dinosaurs.

cloze.exp: look at 看著…；主詞 He 用 looks。sees 後面不接 at。
many + 複數名詞：many pictures。
not ... anymore 不再…。雨停後他不再難過了。
want to + 原形動詞：want to visit。

qs.q: Why can't Leo play basketball?
qs.exp: It is rainy today, so Leo can't play basketball.

qs.q: What is Leo's book about?
qs.exp: an old book about dinosaurs.

qs.q: What does Leo want to do this weekend?
qs.exp: He wants to visit the science museum this weekend.

tr: 今天下雨，所以里歐不能去公園打籃球。
他有點難過。
他坐在窗邊看著雨。
媽媽說：「你何不看本書呢？」
里歐找到一本關於恐龍的舊書。
這本書有很多圖片。
里歐知道了有些恐龍跟房子一樣高！
他看了兩個小時的書。
雨停的時候，里歐已經不難過了。
他想這個週末去科學博物館看恐龍。

passages.title: Healthy Habits
passages.text:
Do you want to be healthy? Here are some easy ways.
First, eat more fruit and vegetables. They are good {for} your body. Second, drink water, not soda. Soda has too much sugar. Third, exercise every day. You can ride a bike, jump rope, or {swim}. Fourth, go to bed early. Children need about ten hours of sleep.
If you {follow} these habits, you will feel strong and happy!

cloze.exp: be good for... 對…有益。
can 後面接原形動詞，與 ride、jump 並列：swim。
follow habits 遵守（養成）這些習慣。

qs.q: Why should we drink water, not soda?
qs.exp: Soda has too much sugar.

qs.q: Which is NOT a way to exercise in the passage?
qs.exp: 文中提到騎腳踏車、跳繩、游泳，沒有打籃球。

qs.q: How many hours of sleep do children need?
qs.exp: Children need about ten hours of sleep.

tr: 你想要健康嗎？
這裡有一些簡單的方法。
第一，多吃水果和蔬菜。
它們對你的身體很好。
第二，喝水，不要喝汽水。
汽水含有太多糖。
第三，每天運動。
你可以騎腳踏車、跳繩或游泳。
第四，早點睡覺。
兒童大約需要十個小時的睡眠。
如果你養成這些習慣，你會覺得強壯又快樂！

passages.title: A Day at the Beach
passages.text:
Last Sunday, my family {went} to the beach. The weather was hot and sunny. My dad and I swam in the sea. My sister made a sandcastle.
At noon, we ate sandwiches under a big umbrella. Then I found {some} pretty shells. I put them in my bag. In the evening, we watched the sun go down. The sky was orange and red. I was tired, {but} I was very happy. I {want} to go there again.

cloze.exp: Last Sunday 是過去時間，用過去式 went。
肯定句、可數複數 shells 用 some。
累了「但是」很開心，前後語意轉折用 but。
主詞 I，後面接 to go，用 want。

qs.q: What did the writer's sister do at the beach?
qs.exp: My sister made a sandcastle.

qs.q: Where did they eat lunch?
qs.exp: we ate sandwiches under a big umbrella.

qs.q: How did the writer feel at the end of the day?
qs.exp: I was tired, but I was very happy.

tr: 上星期日，我們全家去海邊。
天氣又熱又晴朗。
爸爸和我在海裡游泳。
我妹妹堆了一座沙堡。
中午，我們在一把大陽傘下吃三明治。
然後我找到一些漂亮的貝殼。
我把它們放進我的包包。
傍晚，我們看著太陽下山。
天空是橘色和紅色的。
我很累，但是很開心。
我想要再去那裡。

passages.title: My Pet Rabbit
passages.text:
I have a pet rabbit. Her name is Snowy. She is white and has long ears. She is very {cute}.
Every morning, I give Snowy carrots and water. She likes carrots very much. After school, I play with her in the living room. She can jump very {high}. On weekends, I clean her house. My mom {helps} me. Snowy is my best friend. I love her a {lot}.

cloze.exp: be 動詞 is 後面接形容詞 cute。
跳得很高：jump high。
主詞 My mom 是第三人稱單數，用 helps。
I love her a lot. 我非常愛她。

qs.q: What color is Snowy?
qs.exp: She is white and has long ears.

qs.q: What does Snowy like to eat?
qs.exp: She likes carrots very much.

qs.q: Who helps the writer clean Snowy's house?
qs.exp: My mom helps me.

tr: 我有一隻寵物兔。
她的名字叫小雪。
她是白色的，有長長的耳朵。
她非常可愛。
每天早上，我給小雪紅蘿蔔和水。
她非常喜歡紅蘿蔔。
放學後，我在客廳和她玩。
她可以跳得很高。
週末時，我會清理她的家。
我媽媽會幫我。
小雪是我最好的朋友。
我非常愛她。

passages.title: The Class Trip
passages.text:
Last Friday, the sixth graders at Sunshine Elementary School went on a class trip to a farm. When they arrived, the farmer, Mr. Wang, showed them around.
First, they {fed} the cows and sheep. Some students were afraid at first, but soon they had fun. Next, they picked strawberries. The strawberries were red and sweet. Mr. Wang said, "Don't eat too {many}. Save some for your family!"
At lunch, they ate rice balls under a big tree. In the afternoon, they learned how to make ice cream with fresh milk. It was {harder} than they thought, but it tasted great. On the bus home, everyone was tired {but} happy.

cloze.exp: Last Friday 為過去，feed（餵）的過去式是 fed。
strawberries 可數，too many 太多（顆）。
後面有 than，用比較級 harder。
「累，但很開心」語意轉折：tired but happy。

qs.q: Where did the students go last Friday?
qs.exp: went on a class trip to a farm.

qs.q: Why did Mr. Wang say "Don't eat too many"?
opts: He wanted them to save some for their families.
qs.exp: Save some for your family!

qs.q: What did the students learn to make?
qs.exp: they learned how to make ice cream with fresh milk.

qs.q: How did the students feel on the bus home?
qs.exp: everyone was tired but happy.

tr: 上星期五，陽光國小的六年級生到農場校外教學。
他們到達時，農夫王先生帶他們四處參觀。
首先，他們餵了乳牛和綿羊。
有些學生一開始很害怕，但很快就玩得很開心。
接著，他們去採草莓。
草莓又紅又甜。
王先生說：「不要吃太多。
留一些給你們的家人！」
午餐時，他們在一棵大樹下吃飯糰。
下午，他們學習用新鮮牛奶做冰淇淋。
這比他們想的還難，但是吃起來很棒。
在回家的公車上，大家都很累，但是很開心。

passages.title: Grandpa's Garden
passages.text:
My grandpa lives in the country. He has a small garden behind his house. Every summer vacation, I {stay} with him for two weeks.
Grandpa grows tomatoes, corn, and sweet potatoes. Every morning, we get up early to water the plants {before} it gets too hot. Grandpa tells me that plants are like people. "They need water, sunlight, and love," he says.
This summer, I planted my own tomato plant. I took care of it every day. At the end of my stay, I picked three red tomatoes. Grandpa cooked them with eggs for dinner. It was the most {delicious} dish I have ever eaten, because I grew the tomatoes {myself}.

cloze.exp: Every summer vacation 表習慣，主詞 I 用原形 stay。
趁天氣變太熱「之前」澆水：before it gets too hot。
自己種的番茄做成的菜，是吃過「最好吃」的：the most delicious。
反身代名詞 myself：我自己（親手）種的。

qs.q: Where does the writer's grandpa live?
qs.exp: My grandpa lives in the country.

qs.q: Why do they water the plants early in the morning?
opts: Because it gets too hot later.
Because it rains in the afternoon.
qs.exp: water the plants before it gets too hot.

qs.q: What did Grandpa do with the three tomatoes?
opts: He gave them to a friend.
qs.exp: Grandpa cooked them with eggs for dinner.

qs.q: Why was the dish so delicious to the writer?
qs.exp: because I grew the tomatoes myself.

tr: 我的爺爺住在鄉下。
他家後面有一個小菜園。
每年暑假，我都會去他那裡住兩個星期。
爺爺種番茄、玉米和地瓜。
每天早上，我們趁天氣變太熱之前，早早起床幫植物澆水。
爺爺告訴我，植物就像人一樣。
「它們需要水、陽光和愛。」他說。
今年夏天，我種了一棵自己的番茄。
我每天都照顧它。
在住宿的最後，我摘了三顆紅番茄。
爺爺把它們和蛋一起煮成晚餐。
那是我吃過最好吃的一道菜，因為番茄是我自己種的。

passages.title: A New Student
passages.text:
There is a new student in Ruby's class. His name is Kenji, and he is from Japan. On his first day, Kenji didn't {say} much. He sat alone at lunch time.
Ruby thought, "He must feel lonely." So she walked over and asked, "Can I sit with you?" Kenji smiled. He spoke a little Chinese and some English.
Ruby {showed} him around the school and taught him some Chinese words. Kenji taught her how to {fold} paper cranes. Now they are good friends. Ruby learned that a small act of kindness can make a big {difference}.

cloze.exp: didn't 後面接原形動詞：didn't say much 話不多。
過去發生的事，show 的過去式 showed；show sb. around 帶某人參觀。
fold paper cranes 摺紙鶴。
make a difference 帶來改變、產生影響。

qs.q: Where is Kenji from?
qs.exp: he is from Japan.

qs.q: Why did Ruby sit with Kenji?
qs.exp: Ruby thought, "He must feel lonely."

qs.q: What did Kenji teach Ruby?
qs.exp: Kenji taught her how to fold paper cranes. 教中文字的是 Ruby。

qs.q: What did Ruby learn?
opts: A small act of kindness can make a big difference.
qs.exp: a small act of kindness can make a big difference.

tr: 露比的班上來了一位新同學。
他叫健司，來自日本。
第一天，健司話不多。
午餐時間他一個人坐著。
露比心想：「他一定覺得很寂寞。」
所以她走過去問：「我可以和你一起坐嗎？」
健司笑了。
他會說一點中文和一些英文。
露比帶他參觀學校，還教他一些中文字詞。
健司教她怎麼摺紙鶴。
現在他們是好朋友。
露比學到，一個小小的善舉可以帶來很大的改變。

passages.title: Sports Day
passages.text:
Last Wednesday was Sports Day at our school. All the students wore their sports clothes and sat on the playground. The principal gave a short speech, and then the games began.
My class was in the relay race. I was the last runner, so I felt very {nervous}. When my classmate gave me the stick, our team was in third place. I ran as fast as I {could}. Everyone shouted my name. At the end, I passed one runner, and we got second place!
Our teacher {was} very proud of us. After the race, we drank cold water and took a class photo. It was a day I will never {forget}.

cloze.exp: 最後一棒壓力很大，所以「緊張」nervous。
as fast as I could 盡我所能地快；過去式用 could。
主詞 Our teacher 單數，過去時間用 was。
will 後面接原形動詞 forget。

qs.q: Which race was the writer's class in?
qs.exp: My class was in the relay race.

qs.q: Why did the writer feel nervous?
opts: Because the writer was the last runner.
Because the writer lost the stick.
qs.exp: I was the last runner, so I felt very nervous.

qs.q: What place did the team get in the end?
qs.exp: we got second place!

qs.q: What did the class do after the race?
opts: They drank cold water and took a photo.
qs.exp: we drank cold water and took a class photo.

tr: 上星期三是我們學校的運動會。
所有學生都穿著運動服，坐在操場上。
校長發表了簡短的演說，然後比賽開始了。
我們班參加大隊接力。
我是最後一棒，所以我覺得非常緊張。
當同學把接力棒交給我時，我們隊是第三名。
我盡全力跑得最快。
大家都喊著我的名字。
最後，我超越了一位跑者，我們得到第二名！
我們老師非常以我們為榮。
比賽結束後，我們喝了冰水，拍了一張班級合照。
這是我永遠不會忘記的一天。

passages.title: Making Dumplings
passages.text:
Every year before Chinese New Year, my family makes dumplings together. This year, my grandma taught me {how} to make them.
First, we mixed pork, cabbage, and green onions in a big bowl. Then Grandma showed me how to put the meat in the middle of the dumpling skin and close it. My first dumpling looked {like} a small ball, and everyone laughed. I tried again and again. After thirty minutes, my dumplings looked much {better}.
We made more than one hundred dumplings. We boiled some for dinner and put the rest in the freezer. They were delicious. Grandma said I did a good job, and I felt very {proud}.

cloze.exp: how to + 原形動詞：如何做…。
look like + 名詞：看起來像…。
much 修飾比較級：much better 好多了。
被稱讚後覺得驕傲 proud。

qs.q: Who taught the writer to make dumplings?
qs.exp: my grandma taught me how to make them.

qs.q: Why did everyone laugh?
opts: The writer's first dumpling looked like a small ball.
qs.exp: My first dumpling looked like a small ball, and everyone laughed.

qs.q: What did they do with the dumplings they didn't eat?
opts: They put them in the freezer.
qs.exp: put the rest in the freezer.

qs.q: Which is NOT in the dumplings?
qs.exp: 內餡是 pork, cabbage, green onions，沒有 beef。

tr: 每年過年前，我們家都會一起包水餃。
今年，奶奶教我怎麼包。
首先，我們在一個大碗裡把豬肉、高麗菜和蔥拌在一起。
接著奶奶示範怎麼把肉放在水餃皮中間再包起來。
我包的第一顆水餃看起來像一顆小球，大家都笑了。
我試了一次又一次。
三十分鐘後，我的水餃看起來好多了。
我們包了一百多顆水餃。
我們煮了一些當晚餐，剩下的放進冷凍庫。
它們很好吃。
奶奶說我做得很好，我覺得非常驕傲。

passages.title: My New Neighbor
passages.text:
Last month, a new family moved into the house next to mine. They have a girl named Emma. She is twelve years old, just like me. On the first day, I saw her in front of her house. She looked a little shy, so I {said} hello to her. She smiled and told me she came from Canada.
Now Emma and I go to school {together} every morning. She is good at English, and I am good at math, so we often {help} each other with our homework. On weekends, we ride our bikes to the park near our street. Emma likes to take pictures of birds and flowers there.
Emma's mother is very kind. She sometimes {makes} cookies for us. Last Sunday, Emma taught me how to make them. They were not very pretty, {but} they were delicious! I am happy to have a new neighbor and a new {friend}.

cloze.exp: say hello to sb. 向某人打招呼，過去式為 said。
go to school together 一起上學。
主詞 we 搭配頻率副詞 often，用原形動詞 help。help each other with... 互相幫忙…
主詞 She 為第三人稱單數、敘述習慣（sometimes），用 makes。
「不太好看，但很好吃」前後語意相反，用 but。
全文描述兩人成為好朋友：a new neighbor and a new friend。

qs.q: Where did Emma come from?
qs.exp: 第一段最後：She ... told me she came from Canada.

qs.q: How do the writer and Emma help each other?
opts: Emma helps with English, and the writer helps with math.
Emma helps with math, and the writer helps with English.
They both help each other with science.
Emma's mother helps them with homework.
qs.exp: She is good at English, and I am good at math, so we often help each other.

qs.q: What does Emma like to do in the park?
opts: Take pictures of birds and flowers.
qs.exp: Emma likes to take pictures of birds and flowers there.

qs.q: What do we know about the cookies they made last Sunday?
opts: They didn't look nice, but they tasted good.
They looked nice and tasted good.
They were too sweet to eat.
qs.exp: They were not very pretty, but they were delicious!

tr: 上個月，有一戶新的人家搬進我家隔壁的房子。
他們有一個女兒叫艾瑪。
她十二歲，跟我一樣。
第一天，我看到她在她家門前。
她看起來有點害羞，所以我跟她打招呼。
她笑了，告訴我她來自加拿大。
現在艾瑪和我每天早上一起上學。
她擅長英文，我擅長數學，所以我們常常互相幫忙寫功課。
週末時，我們騎腳踏車到我們街附近的公園。
艾瑪喜歡在那裡拍鳥和花的照片。
艾瑪的媽媽人很好。
她有時會做餅乾給我們吃。
上星期日，艾瑪教我怎麼做餅乾。
它們不太好看，但是很好吃！
我很高興有了一個新鄰居，也多了一個新朋友。

passages.title: A Busy Saturday
passages.text:
Kevin usually gets up late on weekends, but last Saturday was different. He {got} up at six thirty because his family had a lot of things to do.
First, Kevin and his father cleaned the living room and washed the car. Then his mother asked him to go to the supermarket with her. They {bought} some eggs, milk, apples, and a big fish for dinner.
In the afternoon, Kevin's grandparents came to visit. Kevin played chess with his grandfather, and he {lost} three games in a row. His grandmother laughed and said, "Don't worry. Your grandfather has played chess for fifty years."
In the evening, the whole family cooked dinner together. Kevin's job was to {wash} the vegetables. After dinner, Kevin was so {tired} that he went to bed at nine. It was a busy day, {but} Kevin felt very happy.

cloze.exp: last Saturday 為過去時間，用過去式 got。
在超市「買了」東西，buy 的過去式 bought（注意與 brought 帶來 區分）。
奶奶安慰他 Don't worry，可知他「輸了」：lose → lost。
be 動詞 + to + 原形動詞：His job was to wash...。
so...that... 太…以致於…；累到九點就去睡，用 tired。
「很忙，但很快樂」語意轉折，用 but。

qs.q: What time did Kevin get up last Saturday?
qs.exp: He got up at six thirty.

qs.q: Who did Kevin go to the supermarket with?
qs.exp: his mother asked him to go to the supermarket with her.

qs.q: Why did Kevin's grandmother say "Don't worry"?
opts: Kevin was too tired to cook.
qs.exp: Kevin 下棋連輸三盤（lost three games in a row），奶奶才安慰他。

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT true?
opts: Kevin went to bed at ten.
Kevin washed the car with his father.
Kevin's grandfather has played chess for a long time.
qs.exp: 文中說 he went to bed at nine，九點就寢，不是十點。

tr: 凱文週末通常很晚起床，但上星期六不一樣。
他六點半就起床了，因為家裡有很多事要做。
首先，凱文和爸爸打掃客廳、洗車。
然後媽媽要他陪她去超市。
他們買了一些蛋、牛奶、蘋果，還有一條大魚當晚餐。
下午，凱文的爺爺奶奶來拜訪。
凱文和爺爺下西洋棋，結果連輸了三盤。
奶奶笑著說：「別擔心。
你爺爺已經下了五十年的棋了。」
傍晚，全家人一起煮晚餐。
凱文的工作是洗菜。
晚餐後，凱文累到九點就上床睡覺了。
這是忙碌的一天，但凱文覺得非常快樂。

passages.title: Lunch Time at School
passages.text:
Many students in Taiwan eat lunch at school. At Lily's school, lunch {time} starts at twelve o'clock. Students take turns to bring the food from the kitchen to their classroom.
Today it is Lily's turn. She and two classmates carry the rice, soup, and dishes {carefully}. Their teacher, Mr. Lin, always says, "Don't run with the soup. It's hot!"
Lily likes most of the food, but she doesn't like green peppers. Mr. Lin tells the class not to {waste} food. "Try one bite," he says. "Vegetables are good for your body." Lily tries a small piece. It is not as bad as she thinks.
After lunch, everyone {cleans} the tables and puts the bowls back. Then they take a short nap. Lily thinks lunch time is {fun} because she can talk with her friends {while} they eat.

cloze.exp: lunch time 午餐時間，與後文 starts at twelve o'clock 呼應。
湯很燙不能跑，所以要「小心地」搬：carefully。
老師要大家試一口，意思是不要「浪費」食物：waste。
everyone 視為第三人稱單數，現在式用 cleans。
可以和朋友聊天，所以覺得午餐時間「好玩」：fun。
while 當…的時候（同時進行）：邊吃邊聊。

qs.q: What time does lunch time start at Lily's school?
qs.exp: lunch time starts at twelve o'clock.

qs.q: Why does Mr. Lin say "Don't run with the soup"?
opts: Because the soup is not delicious.
Because the classroom is far away.
qs.exp: Don't run with the soup. It's hot!

qs.q: How does Lily feel after she tries the green pepper?
opts: It is not as bad as she thinks.
She wants to eat all of it.
qs.exp: It is not as bad as she thinks. 沒有她想像中那麼糟。

qs.q: What do students do right after they clean the tables?
qs.exp: Then they take a short nap. 接著午睡。

tr: 台灣很多學生在學校吃午餐。
在莉莉的學校，午餐時間從十二點開始。
學生輪流把食物從廚房搬到教室。
今天輪到莉莉。
她和兩位同學小心地搬飯、湯和菜。
他們的老師林老師總是說：「拿著湯不要跑。
很燙！」
莉莉喜歡大部分的菜，但是她不喜歡青椒。
林老師告訴全班不要浪費食物。
「試一口看看。」他說。
「蔬菜對你們的身體很好。」
莉莉試了一小塊。
沒有她想像中那麼難吃。
午餐後，每個人都把桌子擦乾淨，把碗放回去。
然後他們睡個短短的午覺。
莉莉覺得午餐時間很有趣，因為她可以一邊吃一邊和朋友聊天。

passages.title: Helping at the Library
passages.text:
This semester, I joined the library helpers' club at school. Every Tuesday and Thursday, I spend my lunch break in the library. My job is to put the returned books back on the {right} shelves.
At first, it was not easy. There are thousands of books in our library, and each book has a number on it. I had to learn how the numbers {work}. Ms. Lin, our librarian, was very patient. She explained everything to me again and again.
Now I can find any book in less {than} a minute. Last week, a seventh grader was looking for a book about dinosaurs, and I helped her find it. She said thank you with a big smile. That made me feel {useful}.
Being a library helper takes time, {but} I have learned a lot. I also read more books than before, {because} I always see interesting new titles on the shelves.

cloze.exp: 把書放回「正確的」書架：the right shelves。
間接問句 how the numbers work，主詞 numbers 複數用 work。
less than a minute 不到一分鐘。
幫助別人讓我覺得自己「有用」。
花時間「但是」學到很多，語意轉折。
讀更多書的原因：因為常看到有趣的新書。

qs.q: When does the writer help in the library?
opts: During lunch break on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
qs.exp: Every Tuesday and Thursday, I spend my lunch break in the library.

qs.q: Who is Ms. Lin?
qs.exp: Ms. Lin, our librarian, was very patient.

qs.q: What was hard for the writer at first?
opts: Learning how the book numbers work.
qs.exp: each book has a number on it. I had to learn how the numbers work.

qs.q: What is one good thing the writer got from the job?
opts: The writer reads more books than before.
The writer has more free time.
The writer can take books home for free.
qs.exp: I also read more books than before.

tr: 這學期，我參加了學校的圖書館小幫手社。
每週二和週四，我都在圖書館度過午休。
我的工作是把歸還的書放回正確的書架上。
一開始，這並不容易。
我們圖書館有好幾千本書，每本書上都有一個編號。
我必須學會這些編號是怎麼運作的。
我們的圖書館員林老師非常有耐心。
她一次又一次地向我解釋每件事。
現在我可以在一分鐘內找到任何一本書。
上星期，一位七年級生在找一本關於恐龍的書，我幫她找到了。
她帶著大大的笑容向我道謝。
那讓我覺得自己很有用。
當圖書館小幫手要花時間，但我學到了很多。
我也比以前讀更多書，因為我總是在書架上看到有趣的新書。

passages.title: Grandpa's New Smartphone
passages.text:
Last month, my grandpa got his first smartphone. He was excited, but he didn't know how to use it. He asked me to {teach} him.
First, I showed him how to make video calls. Now he calls my aunt in Kaohsiung every evening. He can see her face and talk to her for a long time. Next, I taught him how to take photos. He likes taking pictures of the flowers in his garden. Sometimes he takes {too} many pictures, and his phone gets full.
The {hardest} part was typing. Grandpa's fingers are big, and the keys on the screen are small. So I showed him how to send voice messages {instead}. Now he sends me voice messages every day. He usually says, "Eat more and study hard!"
Teaching Grandpa was fun. I learned that older people can learn new things, {too}. They just need more time and someone who is {patient}.

cloze.exp: ask sb. to + 原形動詞：要求某人去做…。
too many 太多。
the + 最高級：最難的部分。
改用語音訊息「代替」打字：instead。
肯定句句尾的「也」用 too。
需要一個「有耐心的」人教他們。

qs.q: Who does Grandpa call every evening?
qs.exp: he calls my aunt in Kaohsiung every evening.

qs.q: Why does Grandpa's phone get full?
qs.exp: Sometimes he takes too many pictures, and his phone gets full.

qs.q: Why does Grandpa send voice messages?
opts: Typing on the small screen is hard for him.
qs.exp: Grandpa's fingers are big, and the keys on the screen are small.

qs.q: What did the writer learn?
opts: Older people can learn new things, too.
Smartphones are bad for older people.
qs.exp: I learned that older people can learn new things, too.

tr: 上個月，我爺爺買了他的第一支智慧型手機。
他很興奮，但不知道怎麼使用。
他請我教他。
首先，我教他怎麼視訊通話。
現在他每天傍晚都打給在高雄的姑姑。
他可以看到她的臉，和她聊很久。
接著，我教他怎麼拍照。
他喜歡拍他花園裡的花。
有時候他拍太多照片，手機就滿了。
最難的部分是打字。
爺爺的手指很粗，螢幕上的按鍵卻很小。
所以我教他改傳語音訊息。
現在他每天都傳語音訊息給我。
他通常會說：「多吃一點，要用功讀書！」
教爺爺很有趣。
我學到年長的人也能學新東西。
他們只是需要多一點時間，以及一個有耐心的人。

passages.title: The Lost Wallet
passages.text:
Last Friday, Jason was waiting for the bus after school when he noticed a brown wallet on the ground. He picked it up and looked inside. There was some money, a student card, and a photo of an old woman. The card {belonged} to a girl named Amy Chen from another junior high school.
Jason's first thought was to keep the money, because he wanted to buy a new video game. {However}, when he looked at the photo again, he changed his mind. "Maybe the photo is {important} to her," he thought.
Jason took the wallet to the police station near the bus stop. The police officer called Amy's school, and an hour later, Amy and her mother arrived. Amy almost {cried} when she saw the wallet. She explained that the woman in the photo was her grandmother, who passed away last year. It was the only picture she had of the two of them together.
Amy's mother wanted to give Jason some money as a thank-you gift, but he {refused}. "I'm just glad you got it back," he said. On his way home, Jason felt {proud} of himself. He learned that doing the right thing can make someone's day {much} better.

cloze.exp: belong to 屬於。學生證「屬於」Amy Chen。
原本想留下錢，「然而」看到照片後改變主意，用 However 表轉折。
照片對她可能很「重要」：important。
看到失而復得的皮夾，激動得「差點哭了」：almost cried。
後面說 I'm just glad you got it back，可知他「拒絕」收錢：refused。
be/feel proud of oneself 以自己為傲。
修飾比較級 better 要用 much，不能用 very。

qs.q: What was NOT in the wallet?
opts: A photo of an old woman.
qs.exp: 皮夾裡有錢、學生證和照片；video game 是 Jason 想買的東西。

qs.q: Why did Jason change his mind about keeping the money?
opts: He thought the photo might be important to the owner.
He already had a new video game.
His mother told him to return it.
qs.exp: "Maybe the photo is important to her," he thought.

qs.q: Who was the woman in the photo?
qs.exp: the woman in the photo was her grandmother.

qs.q: What kind of person is Jason?
qs.exp: 他歸還皮夾且拒收謝禮，是誠實又善良的人。

tr: 上星期五，傑森放學後在等公車時，注意到地上有一個棕色的皮夾。
他把它撿起來，看了看裡面。
裡面有一些錢、一張學生證，和一張老婦人的照片。
這張學生證屬於另一所國中一位名叫陳艾咪的女生。
傑森的第一個念頭是把錢留下來，因為他想買一款新的電玩。
然而，當他再看一次照片時，他改變了主意。
「也許這張照片對她很重要。」他心想。
傑森把皮夾拿到公車站附近的警察局。
警察打電話到艾咪的學校，一個小時後，艾咪和她媽媽趕到了。
艾咪看到皮夾時差點哭出來。
她解釋說，照片裡的女士是她去年過世的奶奶。
那是她唯一一張和奶奶的合照。
艾咪的媽媽想給傑森一些錢當謝禮，但是他拒絕了。
「我只是很高興妳把它拿回來了。」他說。
在回家的路上，傑森為自己感到驕傲。
他學到，做對的事可以讓別人的一天變得好很多。

passages.title: A Night at the Night Market
passages.text:
Night markets are one of the most popular places in Taiwan. Last summer, my cousin Mike visited Taiwan from the United States for the first time, and I took him to a famous night market in Taipei.
As soon as we arrived, Mike was {surprised} by the crowds. "Are there always so many people here?" he asked. I told him that night markets are usually busiest on weekends.
We walked from one food stand to {another}. Mike tried bubble tea, fried chicken, and oyster omelets. He loved all of them. Then I asked him to try stinky tofu. He looked at it and said, "It smells terrible! Do I really have to eat it?" I {laughed} and told him to try just one piece. To his surprise, it tasted much better than it {smelled}.
Besides food, there were also many games. Mike played a ring toss game and {won} a small toy bear for his little sister.
Before we went home, Mike said, "The night market is the best part of my trip. I want to come back again {next} year." I was glad he had {such} a good time in Taiwan.

cloze.exp: 第一次看到人潮，感到「驚訝」：be surprised by...。
from one... to another 從一個…到另一個。
表弟誇張的反應讓作者「笑了」。
臭豆腐「吃起來比聞起來好得多」：tasted better than it smelled。
玩套圈圈遊戲「贏得」小熊：win → won。
想「明年」再來：next year。
such + a + 形容詞 + 名詞：such a good time。

qs.q: When are night markets usually the busiest?
qs.exp: night markets are usually busiest on weekends.

qs.q: How did Mike feel about stinky tofu after he tried it?
opts: It tasted better than he expected.
It tasted as terrible as it smelled.
He didn't want to try it at all.
He thought it was too sweet.
qs.exp: To his surprise, it tasted much better than it smelled.

qs.q: Who was the toy bear for?
qs.exp: won a small toy bear for his little sister.

qs.q: What is this story mainly about?
opts: A cousin's first visit to a Taiwanese night market.
How to win a ring toss game.
qs.exp: 全文描述表弟 Mike 第一次逛台灣夜市的經驗。

tr: 夜市是台灣最受歡迎的地方之一。
去年夏天，我的表弟麥克第一次從美國來台灣玩，我帶他去台北一個有名的夜市。
我們一到，麥克就被人潮嚇到了。
「這裡總是有這麼多人嗎？」他問。
我告訴他，夜市通常在週末最熱鬧。
我們從一個小吃攤逛到另一個。
麥克吃了珍珠奶茶、炸雞和蚵仔煎。
他全部都很喜歡。
接著我要他試試臭豆腐。
他看著它說：「聞起來好可怕！
我真的要吃嗎？」
我笑了，叫他只試一塊就好。
令他驚訝的是，它吃起來比聞起來好太多了。
除了食物，還有很多遊戲。
麥克玩了套圈圈，贏到一隻小熊玩偶要送給他妹妹。
回家前，麥克說：「夜市是我這趟旅行最棒的部分。
我明年還想再來。」
我很高興他在台灣玩得這麼開心。

passages.title: Plastic in the Ocean
passages.text:
Every year, millions of tons of plastic end up in the ocean. Plastic bags, bottles, and straws are {easy} to use, but they are very hard to get rid of. Some plastic can stay in the ocean for hundreds of years.
This is a big problem for sea animals. Sea turtles often eat plastic bags because they look {like} jellyfish. Some birds feed small pieces of plastic to their babies. Many of these animals get sick or even die.
Plastic can also come back to us. Fish eat tiny pieces of plastic, and then people eat the fish. Scientists are still studying {how} this may affect our health.
So what can we do? There are many simple ways to help. We can bring our own bags {when} we go shopping. We can use cups and bottles that can be used again and again. We can also say "no" to plastic straws. Some students even join beach clean-ups on weekends.
One person's action may seem small. {But} if everyone does a little, together we can make a big {difference}. The ocean is home to many animals, and it is our job to {protect} it.

cloze.exp: 與後面 but they are very hard to get rid of 相對，前面是「容易」使用：easy。
look like 看起來像。塑膠袋看起來像水母。
科學家研究「這會如何影響」健康：how this may affect...。
「去購物時」自備袋子：when we go shopping。
一個人的行動看似微小，「但」大家都做就能帶來改變，語意轉折。
make a difference 產生影響、帶來改變。
海洋是動物的家，我們的責任是「保護」它。

qs.q: Why do sea turtles eat plastic bags?
opts: Birds give the bags to them.
qs.exp: Sea turtles often eat plastic bags because they look like jellyfish.

qs.q: How can plastic "come back to us"?
opts: People eat fish that have eaten plastic.
qs.exp: Fish eat tiny pieces of plastic, and then people eat the fish.

qs.q: Which way to help is NOT mentioned in the passage?
qs.exp: 文中沒有提到回收紙類。

qs.q: What does "get rid of" mean in the first paragraph?
opts: To remove something you don't want.
qs.exp: get rid of 擺脫、除去。

tr: 每年都有數百萬噸的塑膠最後流入海洋。
塑膠袋、瓶子和吸管很方便使用，但很難處理掉。
有些塑膠可以在海裡留存數百年。
這對海洋動物是一個大問題。
海龜常常吃下塑膠袋，因為它們看起來像水母。
有些鳥會把小塊塑膠餵給幼鳥。
這些動物很多會生病，甚至死亡。
塑膠也可能回到我們身上。
魚吃下微小的塑膠碎片，然後人再吃這些魚。
科學家仍在研究這可能如何影響我們的健康。
那麼我們能做什麼呢？
有很多簡單的方法可以幫忙。
購物時我們可以自備袋子。
我們可以使用能重複使用的杯子和瓶子。
我們也可以對塑膠吸管說「不」。
有些學生甚至在週末參加淨灘活動。
一個人的行動看起來可能很小。
但如果每個人都做一點，我們就能一起帶來很大的改變。
海洋是許多動物的家，保護它是我們的責任。

passages.title: Our Class Garden
passages.text:
At the beginning of the school year, our teacher, Mr. Huang, gave our class a small piece of land behind the school building. "Let's grow our own vegetables," he said. Most of us had never planted {anything} before, so we were both excited and worried.
We divided the class into four groups. Each group was {in} charge of one kind of vegetable: lettuce, tomatoes, sweet potatoes, or green beans. My group chose tomatoes. We watered them every morning and pulled out weeds after school.
Things did not always go well. In October, a strong typhoon broke many of our tomato plants. Some classmates wanted to give up, but Mr. Huang told us that {failure} is part of farming. We tied the broken plants to sticks and planted new seeds.
Two months later, our hard work finally paid off. The tomatoes turned red, and the sweet potato group dug up a whole basket of sweet potatoes. We {used} our vegetables to make a big salad and sweet potato soup for the whole class.
The garden taught us many things. We learned how much work goes into the food on our tables. We also learned to work {together} and not to give up easily. {Since} then, I have never left vegetables on my plate. Now I know how {valuable} they are.

cloze.exp: 否定意味（had never）的句子用 anything。
be in charge of 負責…。
老師說「失敗」是種植的一部分。
主動語態、過去時間：We used...。
work together 合作。
Since then + 現在完成式：從那時起。
知道蔬菜多「珍貴」。

qs.q: Which vegetable did the writer's group grow?
qs.exp: My group chose tomatoes.

qs.q: What happened in October?
opts: A typhoon broke many tomato plants.
qs.exp: In October, a strong typhoon broke many of our tomato plants.

qs.q: What does "paid off" mean in the fourth paragraph?
opts: Their hard work brought good results.
qs.exp: pay off 指努力有了成果。

qs.q: How has the writer changed after the garden project?
opts: The writer doesn't leave vegetables on the plate anymore.
The writer wants to be a farmer.
qs.exp: Since then, I have never left vegetables on my plate.

tr: 學年一開始，我們的老師黃老師給了我們班教學大樓後面的一小塊地。
他說：「我們來種自己的蔬菜吧。」
我們大部分的人以前從沒種過任何東西，所以既興奮又擔心。
我們把全班分成四組。
每組負責一種蔬菜：萵苣、番茄、地瓜或四季豆。
我這組選了番茄。
我們每天早上澆水，放學後拔雜草。
事情並不總是順利。
十月時，一個強烈颱風吹斷了我們很多番茄株。
有些同學想放棄，但黃老師告訴我們，失敗是種植的一部分。
我們把折斷的植株綁在棍子上，並種下新的種子。
兩個月後，我們的努力終於有了成果。
番茄變紅了，地瓜組挖出了一整籃地瓜。
我們用自己的蔬菜為全班做了一大盤沙拉和地瓜湯。
這個菜園教了我們很多事。
我們學到餐桌上的食物要花多少功夫。
我們也學會合作、不輕易放棄。
從那之後，我再也沒有把蔬菜剩在盤子裡。
現在我知道它們有多珍貴。

dict.divided: v. 分開（divide 的過去式）

passages.title: A Typhoon Day Off
passages.text:
Last night, the news said that a strong typhoon was coming, and schools would be closed today. My little brother jumped up and down {with} joy. "No school tomorrow!" he shouted. But my parents were busy. They moved the plants inside, closed all the windows, and bought enough food and water.
This morning, the wind was so strong that the trees outside our building were shaking. Heavy rain hit the windows. At about ten o'clock, the power {went} out. Without electricity, we could not watch TV or use the computer. My brother looked bored. "What should we do now?" he asked.
My mom took out an old board game, and we played it together {by} candlelight. My dad told us stories about typhoons when he was a child. He said that his house was once flooded, and he had to stay at his aunt's home for a week. We listened carefully. It was the first time I had heard these stories.
In the afternoon, the power came back. My brother ran to turn on the TV, but I felt a little {disappointed}. The day without electricity was actually fun. A typhoon can be {dangerous}, but this one gave our family a special day. Next time, I hope we can spend time together like this {even} without a typhoon. Of course, I also hope that everyone stays {safe}.

cloze.exp: jump with joy 高興得跳起來。
the power went out 停電了。
by candlelight 在燭光下。
停電好玩，電來了反而有點「失望」。
颱風可能很「危險」，但…（轉折）。
even without a typhoon 即使沒有颱風也…。
stay + 形容詞：stay safe 保持平安。

qs.q: What did the writer's parents do before the typhoon came?
opts: They moved plants inside and bought food and water.
They took the children to school.
qs.exp: They moved the plants inside, closed all the windows, and bought enough food and water.

qs.q: Why couldn't the family watch TV in the morning?
qs.exp: the power went out. Without electricity, we could not watch TV.

qs.q: What happened to the father when he was a child?
qs.exp: his house was once flooded, and he had to stay at his aunt's home for a week.

qs.q: How did the writer feel about the day?
opts: It was special and fun for the family.
It was the worst day ever.
It was too short to enjoy.
qs.exp: The day without electricity was actually fun... this one gave our family a special day.

tr: 昨晚新聞說有一個強烈颱風要來，今天學校停課。
我弟弟高興得跳上跳下。
他大喊：「明天不用上學！」
但我爸媽很忙。
他們把植物搬進屋裡，關上所有窗戶，並買了足夠的食物和水。
今天早上，風大到我們大樓外面的樹都在搖晃。
大雨打在窗戶上。
大約十點時，停電了。
沒有電，我們不能看電視，也不能用電腦。
我弟弟看起來很無聊。
他問：「我們現在要做什麼？」
媽媽拿出一個舊的桌遊，我們在燭光下一起玩。
爸爸告訴我們他小時候遇到颱風的故事。
他說他家曾經淹水，他得在姑姑家住一個星期。
我們仔細地聽。
那是我第一次聽到這些故事。
下午，電來了。
我弟弟跑去打開電視，但我覺得有點失望。
沒有電的這一天其實很好玩。
颱風可能很危險，但這個颱風給了我們家特別的一天。
下一次，我希望即使沒有颱風，我們也能像這樣一起相處。
當然，我也希望大家都平安。

passages.title: Why Teenagers Need More Sleep
passages.zh: 青少年為何需要更多睡眠
passages.text:
Do you often feel sleepy in your first class? If so, you are not {alone}. Many junior high students in Taiwan go to bed late and get up early. Some of them sleep only six hours a night, but doctors say teenagers {need} about eight to ten hours of sleep.
Why is sleep so important? While we are sleeping, our brain is not resting at all. In fact, it is busy organizing what we learned during the day. That is why students who sleep {enough} usually remember things better. Sleep also helps our bodies grow and keeps us healthy.
{Unfortunately}, many students stay up late because of homework, cram school, or their phones. The light from phone screens can make it harder to fall asleep. Some students think they can sleep more on weekends to "pay back" the sleep they lost. However, this does not completely {solve} the problem.
There are some easy ways to sleep better. First, try to go to bed and get up at the same time every day, {even} on weekends. Second, put your phone away at least thirty minutes before bed. Third, avoid drinks with caffeine, such as coffee and some teas, in the afternoon and evening.
Good sleep is not a waste of time. {Instead}, it is one of the best things you can do for your studies and your {health}.

cloze.exp: you are not alone 你並不孤單（很多人也一樣）。lonely 是心理上的寂寞，此處不合。
teenagers 為複數主詞，現在式用原形 need。
睡得「足夠」的學生記憶較好：sleep enough。
接著說學生因功課、補習、手機而熬夜，是負面情況，用 Unfortunately（不幸地）。
週末補眠並不能完全「解決」問題：solve the problem。
even on weekends 即使在週末也（要同時間睡起）。
「不是浪費時間；反而是…」，用 Instead 表「取而代之、反而」。
與前文 Sleep ... keeps us healthy 呼應：your studies and your health。

qs.q: According to doctors, how much sleep do teenagers need each night?
qs.exp: doctors say teenagers need about eight to ten hours of sleep.

qs.q: What does the brain do while we are sleeping?
opts: It organizes what we learned during the day.
qs.exp: it is busy organizing what we learned during the day.

qs.q: What does the writer think about sleeping more on weekends?
opts: It does not fully solve the problem.
It is the best way to sleep better.
It is a waste of time.
It is bad for our bodies.
qs.exp: However, this does not completely solve the problem.

qs.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the writer's suggestions?
opts: Drink coffee in the evening to finish homework.
Go to bed at the same time every day.
Put your phone away before bed.
Avoid drinks with caffeine in the afternoon.
qs.exp: 作者建議下午和晚上「避免」含咖啡因飲料，正好相反。

tr: 你常常在第一節課覺得想睡嗎？
如果是，你並不孤單。
台灣很多國中生晚睡早起。
有些人一晚只睡六個小時，但醫生說青少年大約需要八到十個小時的睡眠。
為什麼睡眠這麼重要？
當我們睡覺時，大腦根本沒有在休息。
事實上，它正忙著整理我們白天學到的東西。
這就是為什麼睡得夠的學生通常記憶比較好。
睡眠也幫助我們的身體成長，並讓我們保持健康。
可惜的是，很多學生因為功課、補習或手機而熬夜。
手機螢幕的光會讓人更難入睡。
有些學生認為可以在週末多睡一點，把失去的睡眠「補回來」。
然而，這並不能完全解決問題。
有一些簡單的方法可以睡得更好。
第一，試著每天在同一時間睡覺和起床，週末也一樣。
第二，睡前至少三十分鐘把手機收起來。
第三，下午和晚上避免喝含咖啡因的飲料，例如咖啡和某些茶。
好好睡覺不是浪費時間。
相反地，這是你能為學業和健康做的最好的事情之一。

passages.title: Learning from Mistakes
passages.text:
When Jenny joined the school basketball team in seventh grade, she was the shortest player. She was also the slowest. During her first game, she missed every shot she {took}. Some students in the crowd laughed at her, and she wanted to {quit}.
That night, Jenny talked with her father. He did not tell her she was great. {Instead}, he asked, "What did you learn today?" Jenny thought for a while. "I learned that I'm too nervous when I shoot," she answered. Her father smiled. "Then you already know what to {work} on."
From then on, Jenny practiced shooting for thirty minutes every morning before school. She also watched videos of good players and wrote down {what} they did. Whenever she made a mistake in a game, she did not feel sorry for herself. She asked herself the same question her father had asked.
Two years later, Jenny was still not the tallest player on the team, but she had become one of the {best} shooters. In the final game of the season, she scored the winning basket in the last five seconds. Her teammates ran to her and lifted her into the air.
After the game, a reporter from the school newspaper asked about her secret. Jenny said, "Mistakes are not the end. They are {lessons}. If you are {willing} to learn from them, you will keep getting better."

cloze.exp: take a shot 投籃；she missed every shot she took 她每一球都沒投進。
被嘲笑後想「放棄」：quit。
爸爸沒有稱讚她，「反而」問她學到什麼：Instead。
work on 致力於改善…。
記下他們「做了什麼」：wrote down what they did（名詞子句）。
兩年苦練後成為「最好的」射手之一：one of the best shooters。
錯誤不是終點，而是「課題／教訓」：lessons。
be willing to + V 願意去做…。

qs.q: Why did Jenny want to quit after her first game?
opts: She missed every shot and some people laughed at her.
Her father told her to stop playing.
She hurt her leg in the game.
qs.exp: she missed every shot... Some students in the crowd laughed at her.

qs.q: What did Jenny's father do that night?
opts: He asked her what she learned.
He told her she was the best player.
He bought her a new basketball.
qs.exp: He did not tell her she was great. Instead, he asked, "What did you learn today?"

qs.q: When did Jenny score the winning basket?
opts: Two years after she joined the team.
One month after she joined the team.
qs.exp: Two years later... In the final game of the season, she scored the winning basket.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the story?
opts: We can grow by learning from our mistakes.
Tall people are better at basketball.
Parents should always praise their children.
Practicing in the morning is the only way to succeed.
qs.exp: 全文主旨：Mistakes are not the end. They are lessons.

tr: 珍妮七年級加入校籃球隊時，是隊上最矮的球員。
她也是跑最慢的。
第一場比賽，她每一球都沒投進。
觀眾席裡有些學生嘲笑她，她想要放棄。
那天晚上，珍妮和爸爸聊天。
爸爸沒有告訴她她很棒。
相反地，他問：「妳今天學到了什麼？」
珍妮想了一會兒。
「我學到我投籃的時候太緊張了。」她回答。
爸爸笑了。
「那妳已經知道要加強什麼了。」
從那時起，珍妮每天上學前練習投籃三十分鐘。
她也看優秀球員的影片，把他們的做法寫下來。
每當她在比賽中犯錯，她不再自怨自艾。
她會問自己爸爸問過的同一個問題。
兩年後，珍妮仍然不是隊上最高的球員，但她已經成為最好的射手之一。
在球季的最後一場比賽，她在最後五秒投進致勝的一球。
隊友們跑向她，把她高高舉起。
賽後，校刊的記者問她成功的祕訣。
珍妮說：「錯誤不是終點。
它們是一堂堂課。
如果你願意從中學習，你就會不斷進步。」

passages.title: Robots in Our Daily Life
passages.text:
Not long ago, robots were things we only saw in movies. Today, they are becoming part of our daily life. In some restaurants, robots carry food to customers' tables. In hospitals, they help doctors {during} operations. At home, robot vacuums clean the floor while people are at work.
Robots are useful because they can do the same job again and again without getting tired. They can also do {dangerous} work, such as checking broken pipes deep underground or looking for people after an earthquake. Because of this, many people believe robots can make our lives safer and easier.
However, not everyone is happy about robots. Some people worry that robots will {take} their jobs. For example, if a factory buys robots to build cars, it may need {fewer} workers. Others worry that people will depend on machines too much and forget how to do simple things by themselves.
Experts say the key is to learn how to work {with} robots, not against them. Robots are good at repeating tasks, but humans are better at creative thinking and understanding other people's feelings. In the future, jobs that need these skills will become even more {important}.
So, will robots change the world? The answer is {probably} yes. The real question is how we will change {along} with them.

cloze.exp: during + 名詞：在手術「期間」。
地底檢查破管、地震後找人，都是「危險」的工作。
擔心機器人「搶走」工作：take their jobs。
workers 為可數名詞，「較少」用 fewer（less 修飾不可數）。
與後面 not against them 對比：學會「與」機器人合作。

tr: 不久之前，機器人還是只會在電影裡看到的東西。
如今，它們正成為我們日常生活的一部分。
在一些餐廳，機器人把食物送到顧客桌上。
在醫院，它們在手術時協助醫生。
在家裡，人們上班時，掃地機器人會清潔地板。
機器人很有用，因為它們能一再重複同樣的工作而不會累。
它們也能做危險的工作，例如檢查地底深處破損的管線，或在地震後搜尋受困的人。
因此，很多人相信機器人能讓我們的生活更安全、更便利。
然而，不是每個人都對機器人感到高興。
有些人擔心機器人會搶走他們的工作。
例如，如果一間工廠買機器人來製造汽車，它可能就需要比較少的工人。
也有人擔心人們會太依賴機器，而忘記怎麼自己做簡單的事。
專家說，關鍵是學會與機器人合作，而不是對抗它們。
機器人擅長重複性的工作，但人類更擅長創意思考和理解他人的感受。
在未來，需要這些能力的工作會變得更加重要。
那麼，機器人會改變世界嗎？
答案很可能是肯定的。
真正的問題是：我們要如何和它們一起改變。

passages.title: The Hidden Cost of Cheap Clothes
passages.text:
Many teenagers love shopping for clothes. Thanks to "fast fashion" brands, it is now possible to buy a T-shirt for less than the price of a lunch box. These stores bring out new styles every week, so shoppers always feel that they {need} something new. But have you ever wondered why these clothes are so cheap?
The answer is not simple. To keep prices low, many companies make their clothes in factories where workers are paid very little. Some of these workers work more than twelve hours a day. In {addition}, making clothes uses a lot of water. It can take about 2,700 liters of water to make just one cotton T-shirt. That is {enough} water for one person to drink for over two years.
The problem does not end after we buy the clothes. Because cheap clothes are often poorly made, they {wear} out quickly. Many people throw them away after wearing them only a few times. Every year, millions of tons of clothes end up in landfills, {where} they may take hundreds of years to break down.
So what can we do? First, think twice before buying. Ask {yourself} whether you really need it. Second, take good care of your clothes so that they last longer. Third, give clothes that you no longer wear to others, or buy second-hand clothes. {Although} these actions seem small, they can make a big difference if many people do them. The next time you see a cheap T-shirt, remember that someone, {somewhere}, may be paying the real price.

tr: 很多青少年喜歡買衣服。
多虧了「快時尚」品牌，現在用不到一個便當的價格就能買到一件T恤。
這些店每週推出新款式，所以購物者總覺得自己需要新東西。
但你是否想過，為什麼這些衣服這麼便宜？
答案並不簡單。
為了壓低價格，許多公司在工資很低的工廠生產衣服。
其中有些工人一天工作超過十二小時。
此外，製作衣服要用掉大量的水。
光是做一件棉T恤，就可能需要大約2,700公升的水。

問題在我們買下衣服後並沒有結束。

每年有數百萬噸的衣服最後進了掩埋場，在那裡它們可能要花幾百年才能分解。
那我們能做什麼呢？
第一，購買前三思。
問問自己是不是真的需要。
第二，好好愛惜衣服，讓它們穿得更久。
第三，把不再穿的衣服送給別人，或購買二手衣。
雖然這些行動看似微小，但如果很多人一起做，就能帶來很大的改變。
下次你看到便宜的T恤時，記得某個地方的某個人，可能正在付出真正的代價。

passages.title: A Summer at the Animal Shelter
passages.text:
Last summer, I volunteered at an animal shelter near my home. Before that, I had never taken care of a pet, so I didn't know what to {expect}. On my first day, the manager, Ms. Chou, showed me around. There were more than sixty dogs and thirty cats, and most of them had been abandoned by their owners.
My job was to clean the cages, give the animals food and water, and walk the dogs. It was hard work, especially on hot afternoons. {However}, the moment I opened the cages, the dogs would run to me and wag their tails. That always made me forget how tired I was.
One dog, a black puppy named Lucky, was very shy. He hid in the corner {whenever} someone came near. Ms. Chou told me that Lucky had been hurt by his former owner. I decided to spend ten minutes with him every day. I didn't try to touch him at first. I just sat quietly and talked to him. After about three weeks, Lucky finally came over and put his head on my leg. I was so {moved} that I almost cried.
At the end of the summer, a young couple {adopted} Lucky. I was sad to say goodbye, but I knew he would have a warm home. This experience taught me that pets are not toys. They are living things that need love and {responsibility}. Before people decide to get a pet, they should think carefully. {Instead} of buying one, they can also consider adopting an animal from a shelter. As the shelter's poster says, "Adopt, don't shop."

tr: 去年暑假，我在家附近的動物收容所當志工。
在那之前，我從來沒有照顧過寵物，所以不知道會遇到什麼。
第一天，負責人周小姐帶我四處參觀。
那裡有超過六十隻狗和三十隻貓，牠們大部分都曾被飼主拋棄。
我的工作是清理籠子、給動物食物和水，還有遛狗。
這是辛苦的工作，尤其是在炎熱的下午。
然而，我一打開籠子，狗狗們就會跑向我、搖著尾巴。
那總讓我忘記自己有多累。
有一隻叫幸運的黑色小狗非常害羞。
每當有人靠近，他就躲在角落。
周小姐告訴我，幸運曾被前飼主傷害。
我決定每天陪他十分鐘。
一開始我沒有試著摸他。
我只是安靜地坐著和他說話。
大約三週後，幸運終於走過來，把頭靠在我的腿上。
我感動得差點哭出來。
暑假結束時，一對年輕夫妻領養了幸運。
要說再見讓我很難過，但我知道他會有一個溫暖的家。
這次經驗讓我明白寵物不是玩具。
牠們是需要愛與責任的生命。
人們決定養寵物前，應該仔細考慮。
與其用買的，他們也可以考慮從收容所領養動物。
就像收容所海報上說的：「以領養代替購買。」
